name: End-to-end target following
question: Do the proposed materials actually hit my target?
purpose: The question the whole pipeline exists to answer.
verdict_rule: the worst grade of its graded metrics
caveats: Random proposals plus the structure-read label filter already reach 64.1%, so most of the end-to-end gain comes from the filter rather than from the search. Reported, not hidden.

Family-free generation on MP-20: the latent refinement steps made the property decoder say the target while pushing the structure decoder into metals (semiconductor share 20% with them, 42-62% without), so the symmetry path uses the target anchor alone.

metrics.name: Target vs true property of the returned structures
metrics.definition: Spearman correlation between the requested target and the reference property of what was returned.
metrics.meaning_good: Asking for more gap returns more gap: the pipeline follows the target.
metrics.meaning_bad: What is returned is unrelated to what was asked for.
metrics.remedy: Check S4 (labels read from the returned structure) first: that is what fixed it here.
metrics.new_dataset_note: On Perov-5 the whole grid has DFT, so this is measured directly. On a user's dataset the equivalent is the hold-out rediscovery test: hide the test split, screen, and compare with its DFT.

metrics.name: Hit rate against a blind draw
metrics.definition: Share of returned candidates within the target window, divided by the same share for random valid compositions.
metrics.meaning_good: The pipeline is far better than guessing.
metrics.meaning_bad: The pipeline is no better than guessing.
metrics.reference_note: Published 9.5% against a 7.7% random baseline (1.2x). Fixed 67.3% (8.7x). Best 83.3% (10.8x), replicate 56.8% (7.4x). A DFT oracle on the same space reaches 21.4%.

metrics.name: Label error against the reference
metrics.definition: Mean absolute difference between the label shown and the reference property of the returned material.
metrics.meaning_good: The promised property is close to the real one.
metrics.meaning_bad: The promised property is far from the real one.
metrics.new_dataset_note: Express in spreads of the target property to transfer between datasets.

metrics.name: Independent judge against the request (family-free generation)
metrics.definition: Mean absolute difference between the requested property and a QUALIFIED independent judge's value for the generated structures, over the whole pool before any consensus selection.  Measures the generator, not the filter.
metrics.meaning_good: Asking for a gap returns structures whose independently judged gap is near it.
metrics.meaning_bad: The generator returns the training set's dominant answer (for MP-20: zero-gap intermetallics) whatever was asked for; the model's own search-latent label hides this by reading the request back.
metrics.remedy: Read the label from the returned structure, not the search latent (S4); use the target anchor with no latent refinement; require an anion; cap the cell at the encoder's max_sites so every candidate can be re-encoded.  Each of these was measured separately on MP-20.
metrics.reference_note: MP-20, 7 targets 0.5-4 eV: search-latent labels + free chemistry 2.00 eV (77 of 84 metals); label read from the returned structure, no refinement, anion required, cell capped: 1.10 eV (24 of 175 metals). Saturates above 3 eV.

metrics.name: Two-judge consensus yield
metrics.definition: Share of the generated pool that BOTH the model's own label, read from the returned structure, and the qualified independent judge place within 0.5 eV of the request.  This is the set a user may be shown.
metrics.meaning_good: Enough candidates survive two independent judges to serve the target.
metrics.meaning_bad: Almost nothing survives both judges: the target is outside what this model and data can serve.
metrics.remedy: Widen the window only with the error band shown; otherwise report the target as not servable (S9).

components.note: check_candidates.py (any candidate table: label from the structure, qualified judge, consensus, two potentials, re-judge, report)
exhaustive_truth.py + generator_vs_truth.py (precision and recall against exact truth)
screen_polymorphs.py --truth test (hold-out rediscovery, the generic replacement on a user dataset)
target_calibration.py (qualified independent judge, fidelity chosen by measurement; --select = two-judge consensus with a charge-balance flag)
instrument_sheet.py (response curve, bias, precision, accuracy with CI, linearity, resolution, range, yield)
generate_to_target.py (the one command: generate -> judge -> relax -> re-judge -> report)
